note: A search that returns nothing is only worth anything if the search itself is written down. Every query below was actually run, on the date given, and its result is recorded whether or not it helped.

sets.g: National Archives · ALL repositories (RSA) — the search this archive should have been running all along
rows: What this archive searched, every time, for the whole project.

What it should have searched. 145 documents unseen. This family left the Cape about 1907 and the entire last generation died in Johannesburg, so their estates are in the TRANSVAAL depot — and NAAIRS offers an “All Archives Repositories” database on the same selection page used every time.

BOOYZEN, JOHANNA MARIA born PRETORIUS (2945/44); BOOYZEN, GEORGE DOWNING MOUNTJOY (1095/48); BOOYZEN, JOHN BARRY (769/52) — the son who signed the 1905 form; BOOYZEN, HENRY JAMES (10/57); and DASCHNER, CATHERINE MARY SOPHIA born BOOYZEN (3734/46).
TAB MHG — two of the 1863 children
BOOYZEN, JAN GERHARDUS LODEWIKUS (O/2899, 1885), the seventh child; and BOOYZEN, JACOBUS NICHOLS (52653, 1923), the eldest and the only “Major” on that list.
TAB MHG — both sons of the second marriage
BOOYZEN, STEPHANUS FRANCOIS (2428/40) and BOOYZEN, GERT JACOBUS (5155/51). Both filed with a z.
Still no estate for Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen née Barry, who died at Mayfair in 1940. Her “Military Pensioner” entry remains unexplained.
TAB CJC — Claims for Compensation, Burghers

The post-war compensation series Open Question 11 has been asking for. It exists. But all seven claims are MARICO, Transvaal — the same district as the Booyzen children who died in the camps — and that is NOT this family, who were Cape. The series is now named correctly; the Cape equivalent is still untouched.

sets.g: National Archives · all repositories — three questions answered by absence
rows: There is NO estate file for Willem Hermanus Booyzen — the man at the centre of the family story — in any archives repository in South Africa. He died at Indwe in 1905 leaving nothing to administer. Set that beside his father's estate of 1884, which recorded "moveables only, such as wearing apparel": two generations, and between them not one estate worth opening.

The testimony ends "the boys initially all got jobs on the mines". No Booyzen mining record appears anywhere in the national archives index. That index covers GOVERNMENT files, not private mining company employment registers, so the negative is a weak one — but every occupation this archive has actually read for these men points elsewhere: boer then mason, tree nurseryman, clerk on the South African Railways. Not one miner among them.
The Johannesburg addresses appear on certificates but nowhere in the archival index.

SAB VWR B645/8/38 (1937): an application by a FARM OWNER AT BARKLY-OOS, R.P.K. BARRY, with his son of the same initials as bywoner. Given this family's Barry–Kolbe naming — Henry James Kolbe Barry, Anthon Rector Kolbe Barry — R.P.K. is very likely Richard Peter Kolbe Barry. That ties the Cape Rebel of Jerpoint, the R. P. Barry who signed the 1915 notice at Manorowen, and five mortgage bonds of 1895–1903 into one landholding man at Barkly East. Tighter, still not proof.
Still no estate anywhere for Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen née Barry, who died at Mayfair in 1940. Her “Military Pensioner” entry is now the longest-standing unexplained thing in the archive.

sets.g: Anglo-Boer War Museum · Cape Rebel register
rows: Every one from the Northern Cape or Griqualand West — Kenhardt, Campbell, Koopmansfontein, Daniel's Kuil, Aberdeen. None from Barkly East, Dordrecht, Wodehouse, Indwe, Lady Grey or Elliot.
Nothing, in any of the fifteen registers.
And two of them are in this family's district: FRED J. BARRY of Ivanhoe, Barkly East / Wodehouse, tried June 1901; and RICHARD PETER BARRY of Jerpoint. Identity unproven.
DANIEL WILLEM SCHOEMAN, plaasboer of CAERLAVEROCK, tried June 1901 — the month before the family married in his house.
J. J. BOOYSEN of HEILBRON, Orange Free State — four hundred miles away, in a different country at the time.

sets.g: National Archives · Cape Town Archives Repository — the searches this archive got wrong first time
rows: The archive previously reported MOUNTJOY as 42 documents of which “all 22 dated 1930 or later were read”. Twenty earlier documents were never opened. They include JAMES MOUNTJOY'S OWN WILLS of 1818 and 1827 and an 1834 Colonial Office memorial from his widow. A filter applied for convenience was written up as if it were the whole search.

KAB MOOC 7/1/104: 42 — MOUNTJOY, JAMES. WILL (1818), joint with SLIER, ANNA CATHARINA, WIFE OF JAMES MOUNTJOY; and MOOC 7/1/104: 43 — the same pair again in 1827, the year he died. Made a year after their 1817 marriage and again at his death.
KAB CO 3972: 17 — “MEMORIALS RECEIVED. THE WIDOW OF J MOUNTJOY. REQUESTING REMISSION OF A FINE”, 1834. A petition in her own voice, seven years after his death.

Five of them mortgage bonds in the name RICHARD PETER BARRY — 1895, 1897 twice, and 1903 twice. A property-holding farmer of that name in the Cape across the war years. Corroboration for the Cape Rebel of Jerpoint, not proof.
The farm name does not appear anywhere in the Cape Town Archives index.

One police constable at Middelburg, 1904–07, filed four times as BOOYSEN and three times as BOOYZEN — twice both ways inside 1905. The best evidence on this site for what the two spellings meant to the people writing them, and it narrows the archive's own reading of the 1905 death form.

sets.g: National Archives · Cape Town Archives Repository (NAAIRS)
rows: All 22 dated 1930 or later were retrieved and read.
The spelling nobody had tried — and two of the four are the Mountjoy–Booysen junction itself, including the 1840 and 1863 death notices.
There is no estate file for Hercules Johannes Mountjoy under any spelling. The estates around him run 1938, 1939, 1943, 1946, 1948 unbroken, so this is an absence, not a gap in the index.
Earliest 1779 — KAB CJ 2633: 29, the testament of Christina Booyzen. The z is a hundred and twenty years older than the war.
No estate for Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer, d. 1843.
No estate for the man at the top of the male line.
All one later man, Willem Johannes Lodewicus.

One near-miss deliberately NOT adopted: KAB NCD 2/1: 49, a notarial will of 1793 for “Jan Booysen, married to the late Magdalena de Beer”. Wrong husband's name, and a wife dead fifty years before ours.
The full-text collection does not cover Cape probate.
Only the 1863 pair. The 1840 death notice is NOT name-indexed and had to be found by interpolating reference numbers across 2,223 images.
Two carried no image. The third, under the spelling MONTYOY, did.

VOID, not informative. This register turns out to be an ORANGE FREE STATE land roll — farm number, morgen, square roods, owners — covering only Winburg, Fauresmith, Vrede, Rouxville, Bethlehem, Bloemfontein, Hoopstad, Kroonstad and Philippolis. A control search on “Dordrecht” returns 670 Cape Rebels and 0 farms.
Sons of Kathleen Barry, killed in service

The archive's own hypothesis — that a son died in the war and that is why she is recorded a “Military Pensioner” — was searched and DISPROVED. The claim was reframed on the page rather than quietly dropped.
Behind a bot check. This archive did not attempt to circumvent it, and records that as the reason.

The enquiry was sent 9 September 2026 to both published addresses. archive@dod.mil.za delivered and has not replied; sandfdoc@mweb.co.za bounced — 550 relay access denied — and that is the address published almost everywhere for the Centre. Recorded because an unanswered letter and an undelivered one are different things.

sets.g: Master of the Supreme Court · the office's own index of death notices, 1834–1912
rows: Particles are indexed separately in this book, so de Beer files under B. The Magdalena entries are Magda Catha du Plessis (1872), Magda de Beer (1865), Magda Vermeulen (1883), Magda Eliz Troskie (1863), Magda Jacomina Nel (1850) and Magda Greef (1839/40). There is NO Magdelena Elisabeth, and nothing dated 1843.
Page 436 onward, alphabetical by christian name with a death-notice number and year against each. A working index of every Booysen death notice reported to the Master between 1834 and 1912.

Not tractable. The archive has no discriminator beyond a trade and a date — “a saddler, in the Cape by March 1817” — and thirteen thousand results cannot be narrowed by that. Recorded so the next person does not repeat it: the way in is a Cape arrival record, not an English birth record.

sets.n: reading the nine located estates, one film at a time
rows: TAB MHG 2945/44 — Anna Johanna Maria Booyzen, born Pretorius

Indexed under her husband George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen as “Spouse”, which is why it was first mistaken for his estate. Sterfkennis, both parents named with a street address, six children with birth dates, all minors. One correction to the archive.
Seven of the nine still to open. References banked on the Sources page so this resumes rather than restarts.

sets.g: FamilySearch · Transvaal probate index, by collection
sets.n: searching the index instead of guessing the film
rows: The whole indexed surname in one Transvaal collection, read in two pages of a hundred and fifty. Confirms the Stephanus Francois file (1940) and the Jan Gerhardus Lodewikus file, and shows that the 1946–1957 estates this archive is chasing are NOT name-indexed — they will have to be found by browsing film.

TAB MHG 1928/42 in full: Joseph Heinrich Daschner, his parents, his wife “born Booyzen”, and eleven children. Read from the image, not the index — the index gives one child's birth year as 1923 where the document says 1922.

Useless as run: the engine treats Mountjoy as fuzzy and returns every Montgomery, Montjoy and Montmorency in the Transvaal. Recorded because the failure is instructive — an exact-match toggle exists for surnames in this API and not for given names.

Charles Bruce Rennie, miner, of Booysens, Johannesburg, died 1936; his pre-deceased wife was a Minnie Bertha Sophia Daschner. No Booyzen connection. Kept as the archive's cleanest example of the Booysens-suburb trap.
